newsitem.title: UK: Gold takes a fresh tumble, then recovers slightly.
newsitem.headline: Gold takes a fresh tumble, then recovers slightly.

text.p: Gold resumed its sharp fall on Wednesday and sentiment crumbled after another round of selling in New York futures, and more losses were on the cards.
Gold slipped $3.50 to $338 an ounce, then rebounded to $340, but analysts said the February low of $336.15 still beckoned.
"It probably wants to go there ($336) just to see if there is any support there," said one London gold dealer.

Many reasons were attached to the slump, including rumours of Bundesbank sales. In fact, gold has been losing value ever since the European central banks began looking at their gold reserves to meet the European Monetary Union entry criteria.
But dealers dismissed talk a central bank might have been involved, and pointed to a triple whammy that rocked sentiment.
"It's probably much less sexy and worrying," said Andy Smith, precious metals analyst at Union Bank of Switzerland.
"Like, say, options positions as price moves down towards put prices. Like the owerwhelming apathy towards gold in the latest rejigging of portfolios."
A third factor was a downturn in gold shares.
Germany's Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Germany had no plans to sell gold to meet the EMU fiscal requirements.
Selling had accelerated on Tuesday as the bullion price breached the critical $345 technical support level.
London gold started quietly steady above $340 on Wednesday, but took another jolt as New York Comex futures were hit again by a mixed bag of sellers including funds and producers.
"It will make a new low below $336 and maybe it will find a base somewhere above $300," said one dealer.
A fall in U.S. housing starts also injected negative sentiment into gold, already wrecked by Friday's higher-than expected March producer price inflation data.
But the market's subsequent recovery to $340 signalled that it might consolidate before probing lower, analysts said.
Other precious metals bucked gold's trend, recovering slightly after an initial fall.
Silver was quoted at $4.77/$4.79, up eight cents on the day, while platinum was $2.10 up at $365.10/$366.10 an ounce.
But platinum was seen heading down to the lower end of its range at $360 which, if broken, might send prices down to $350.
"There is a lot of speculative interest in platinum that has to unwind," said Smith of UBS.
Palladium was indicated barely changed at $150.70/$151.70.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
